institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Institute of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 27, No. 2: % sensitivity in yeasts fungi (blood isolates), January to December 2020. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published December 2021.
reporting: Percent susceptible of yeasts isolated from blood, by species, for the whole hospital (one table, not split by OPD, ward and ICU), with the number of isolates tested per species in parentheses; amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin, micafungin and anidulafungin.
method: Antibiogram as per CLSI M39-A4 (printed "CLSI M-39A4E; 2014"), repeat isolates excluded; interpreted as per CLSI M60 (2018), and the C. albicans breakpoints were used where no species-specific breakpoints are available; C. glabrata voriconazole by an epidemiological cut-off of 0.25 µg/ml (CLSI gives no voriconazole criteria for C. glabrata); amphotericin B is reported as the percentage of isolates with MIC ≤1 µg/ml. The testing method (instrument or cards) is not named in this edition.

verification.note: The page 2 table was parsed from the PDF text layer (pdfplumber word positions; each cell assigned to its drug column by x position, the species label and the number tested read from the label), then every cell and every n was compared by eye with page 2 rendered at scale 4, first as the whole table band and then cut into two halves with the species column kept on both: no differences. Footnote marks and every cell printed with a symbol or text (NA, SDD, "-") were read on the image. The amphotericin B footnote was read at scale 8: the page prints "<" with an underline (read as ≤) where the text layer has "<". The other content (charts, filamentous fungi table and antifungal use chart on pages 2 and 3; pages 1 and 4 to 8) was identified from the text layer and the rendered pages only to describe it in excluded. A second reader re-read every cell and n against the page images on 2026-09-26 (see issues).

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Vol. 27, No. 2 (published December 2021), data January to December 2020, 8 pages. The No. 2 issue of each year carries the mycology, mycobacteriology, virology and serology results (the bacterial antibiogram is in No. 1). Recorded: the page 2 table "% Sensitivity in Yeasts Fungi* (Blood Isolates 2020)", one row per species with the number of isolates tested printed in parentheses (used as n, n_tested) and percent susceptible for amphotericin B, flucytosine, fluconazole, voriconazole, caspofungin, micafungin and anidulafungin. The table covers blood isolates of all locations together and is not split by OPD, ward and ICU, so every row is set "all". Interpreted as per CLSI M60 document, 2018 (heading and footnote), with the C. albicans breakpoints where no species-specific breakpoints are available (noted on the cells concerned); "*Antibiogram as per CLSI M-39A4E; 2014 (Rpt. isolates excluded)": the Vitek 2 YST and E test footnote of earlier editions is gone and no testing method is named; ** amphotericin B as isolates with MIC ≤1 µg/ml (a "<" with an underline); "- = Not done", NA "Guidelines not available" (no such cells); # C. glabrata: fluconazole "100 SDD" (left out) and voriconazole by an epidemiological cut-off of 0.25 µg/ml; ## C. glabrata caspofungin 37.5 for the 8 blood isolates, lower than for the 30 C. glabrata isolates from all specimens, "i.e. 53.3%". Only six species are tabulated, all with organism keys. The paragraph under the table gives the blood cases and share of each species, which can differ from the numbers tested; organism counts from the charts are not recorded (see excluded). The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves the newsletters only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter issue selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "December-2021"). The fungal issues are recorded as their own series (Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, fungal), so their editions trend with each other and are not taken for editions of the bacterial antibiogram published in the first issue of each volume.
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: every cell and every row n re-read from page 2 rendered at scale 4 (the table cut into two halves with the species column kept on both, footnotes cropped separately) and written down before comparing with the file; the seeded sample from sample_cells.py is part of this. All 41 cells and 6 n: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected.

Confirmed: heading and footnote both say CLSI M60 document, 2018 (breakpoints "CLSI M60 (2018)"); "*Antibiogram as per CLSI M-39A4E; 2014" and no testing method named; ** MIC ≤1 µg/ml (underlined "<"); C. glabrata fluconazole "100 SDD" left out with the right note; ## C. glabrata caspofungin 37.5 (8 blood isolates, against 53.3% for 30 isolates from all specimens) recorded. No cells not kept.
